en.title: Avengers: Doomsday Posters Hint at Marvel's Most Controversial MCU Pairing
en.summary: New character posters for the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday have dropped, sparking debate among fans about potential romantic pairings. One specific duo has particularly raised eyebrows, hinting at a storyline many comic purists find questionable.
en.body:
The first wave of character posters for the highly anticipated **Avengers: Doomsday** has arrived, and they’re already setting the internet ablaze with fan theories and some serious head-scratching. While we see familiar faces like **Steve Rogers** wielding Mjölnir and **Thor** with Stormbringer, alongside intriguing combinations such as **Gambit** and **Yelena Belova** with a Sentinel looming, one particular pairing is causing the most stir: **Sue Storm** and **Namor**.

This visual placement of Marvel's First Lady alongside the King of Atlantis has legions of comic fans questioning the creative direction. For those deeply immersed in the **Fantastic Four** lore, **Sue Storm**’s enduring commitment to **Reed Richards** is a cornerstone of her character. The idea of her reciprocating any romantic interest from **Namor**, whose own history with Sue is a complex, often tumultuous affair stretching back to the very inception of the **Fantastic Four** in the 1960s, feels like a narrative leap many aren't ready for.

## A Pairing Born of Memes?

Namor, one of the oldest Marvel characters, predating even Timely Comics, was famously reintroduced into the fold in **Fantastic Four #4** in 1962. His history with Sue Storm has been a recurring element, marked by attraction and conflict, but rarely a stable, reciprocated romance that would supersede her deep bond with Reed. The posters, by placing them together so prominently, could be interpreted as a significant hint towards a potential romantic subplot in **Avengers: Doomsday**. However, many fans argue that this pairing is more a product of internet jokes and out-of-context comic panels than a genuine, established relationship that warrants such focus in a major MCU event film.

## Fan Reactions and MCU Stakes

The community reaction has been swift and divided. While some fans are intrigued by the prospect of a bold, unexpected romance shaking up the MCU, a significant portion views it with skepticism, seeing it as a potentially misguided attempt to capitalize on a niche meme. The stakes are high for **Avengers: Doomsday**, with its massive ensemble cast and the looming threat of **Doctor Doom**. Introducing a controversial romantic pairing could either be a stroke of genius that adds unexpected depth, or a narrative misstep that alienates long-time comic readers. The visual itself, with **Mister Fantastic** standing alongside **Professor Charles Xavier**, hinting at the Illuminati connection, seems to ground the film in established lore, making the Sue/Namor pairing all the more jarring.

## What's Next

**Avengers: Doomsday** is slated for release on December 18, 2026. Whether this poster pairing is a deliberate misdirection, a setup for a complex exploration of attraction and duty, or a nod to a persistent fan theory remains to be seen as more details emerge.

content_raw: The first set of character posters for Avengers: Doomsday has been released and, as you’d expect, they’re a bit of a mess. We’ve got Steve Rogers and Thor , the former with Mjölnir and the latter with Stormbringer. There’s Gambit and Yelena Belova, with a Sentinel looming in the ve even got a swashbuckling Nightcrawler with a very confused-looking M’Baku. View this post on Instagram Perhaps the chief of the Jabari tribe is confused by the way the posters treat Marvel’s First Family, the Fantastic Four . Mister Fantastic stands alongside Professor Charles Xavier, perhaps fittingly, as the two men are academics and members of the Illuminati. More vexing, however, is the fact that Marvel decided to put Sue Storm alongside Namor, king of the deep. And if that pairing makes sense to you, then you probably know the duo only from internet jokes and out-of-context comic book panels. Because those who love the comics know that Sue Storm would never leave Reed Richards, at least not for Prince Namor. The tangled history of Sue Storm and Prince Namor goes all the way back to the beginning of the Fantastic Four, as Stan Lee and Jack Kirby used the comic to bring the Sub-Mariner back into action. Created by Bill Everett, Namor actually predates not just Marvel and Atlas, but even Timely Comics, as he was made for a movie theater promotional comic called Motion Picture Funnies Weekly in 1939. Later that year, he appeared alongside the first Human Torch in Timely’s Marvel Comics #1, making him one of the oldest superheroes. However, he was long gone from the public eye when Fantastic Four #4 hit stands in 1962. So when Johnny Storm burns off the facial hair from a confused unhoused man, readers were just as surprised as he was to find that the man was Namor. Immediately, Namor goes on a rampage against the surface world, and only pauses upon seeing Sue and being overcome by her beauty. Thus, he offers an ultimatum: either Sue marry him or he destroys the world. To save the world, Sue agrees, but the rest of the FF defeat Namor before it comes to that point. So, yes, in their very first meeting, Namor fell for Sue and Sue agreed to marry him, but only as a heroic act to save the world. Nearly every meeting that followed worked according to that same mode: Namor would arrive, make boasts about why he deserves to rule the world, make declarations of love toward Sue, and she would only reciprocate as a strategic move to keep him in line. Yet, for some reason, people online think that Sue’s mere seconds away from dumping Reed to swim off with Namor. Part of the reason is certainly that Namor’s amorous qualities have been accentuated over the past 20 years, a change that coincided with the rise of Tumblr and other sources. Even today, one can easily find people sharing panels from 2012’s Uncanny X-Men #8, when Namor (who was fighting alongside his fellow mutants at the time) seduced a goopy fish lady. Around
